results.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM olist_orders_dataset LIMIT 1001
results.context: Counts every row of the orders table (one row per order), all statuses.

results.question: What is the total revenue?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(price), 2) AS revenue FROM olist_order_items_dataset LIMIT 1001
results.context: Revenue = sum of item prices in BRL, freight excluded, all order statuses (schema rule).

results.question: Which 10 product categories generate the most revenue?
results.sql: SELECT t.product_category_name_english AS category, ROUND(SUM(i.price), 2) AS revenue FROM olist_order_items_dataset AS i JOIN olist_products_dataset AS p ON p.product_id = i.product_id JOIN product_category_name_translation AS t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name GROUP BY t.product_category_name_english ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10
results.context: Revenue = sum of item prices; English category names; items without a translated category are dropped by the inner join.

results.question: How many orders are there in each order status?
results.sql: SELECT order_status AS status, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM olist_orders_dataset GROUP BY order_status ORDER BY orders DESC LIMIT 1001
results.context: One count per order_status, sorted by count.

results.question: Show the number of orders per month in 2017.
results.sql: SELECT STRFTIME(DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', order_purchase_timestamp), '%Y-%m') AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM olist_orders_dataset WHERE YEAR(order_purchase_timestamp) = 2017 GROUP BY month ORDER BY month LIMIT 1001
results.context: Month taken from order_purchase_timestamp; all statuses included.

results.question: Which 5 states have the most unique customers?
results.sql: SELECT customer_state AS state, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS customers FROM olist_customers_dataset GROUP BY customer_state ORDER BY customers DESC LIMIT 5
results.context: Unique customers = distinct customer_unique_id (a person), not customer_id.

results.question: How many payments were made with each payment type?
results.sql: SELECT payment_type, COUNT(*) AS payments FROM olist_order_payments_dataset GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY payments DESC LIMIT 1001
results.context: Counts payment rows (an order can have several payments).

results.question: How many reviews are there for each review score?
results.sql: SELECT review_score AS score, COUNT(*) AS reviews FROM olist_order_reviews_dataset GROUP BY review_score ORDER BY review_score LIMIT 1001
results.context: Counts review rows per score 1-5.

results.question: What is the average delivery time in days for delivered orders?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(DATE_DIFF('DAY', order_purchase_timestamp, order_delivered_customer_date)), 2) AS avg_days FROM olist_orders_dataset WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND NOT order_delivered_customer_date IS NULL LIMIT 1001
results.context: Delivery time = days from purchase to customer delivery; status 'delivered' with a delivery date.

results.question: What percentage of delivered orders arrived after the estimated delivery date?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 2) AS pct_late FROM olist_orders_dataset WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND NOT order_delivered_customer_date IS NULL LIMIT 1001
results.context: Late = delivered timestamp strictly after the estimated delivery date; base is delivered orders with a delivery date.

results.question: How many customers have placed more than one order?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers FROM (SELECT c.customer_unique_id FROM olist_orders_dataset AS o JOIN olist_customers_dataset AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 1) AS t LIMIT 1001
results.context: Customer = customer_unique_id; counts people with 2+ distinct orders, any status.
